from: Distinguish between capacity utilisation and labour productivity.
to: An Otjiwarongo furniture factory could make 1 000 cabinets a month and makes 600, using 20 employees. Explain the difference between its capacity utilisation and its labour productivity.
why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

to: A Windhoek retailer is considering paying a Windhoek courier to run its deliveries, and a Namibian bank is considering opening its own processing office in another country. Explain the difference between outsourcing and offshoring, using these two plans.
why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

from: A workshop reports capacity utilisation of 58% last year and 74% this year, while the number of units it made and sold is the same in both years. Interpret the change.
to: A workshop reports capacity utilisation of 58% last year and 74% this year, while the number of units it made and sold is the same in both years. Explain what the change means for the workshop.
why: Interpret is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain. The answer reads the figures against each other and says what they mean, and it asks for more than one paper part, so no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: A bank is considering a loan application from a manufacturer whose business plan reports capacity utilisation of 88%. Set out the questions the bank should ask about that figure before relying on it, and say what each one would tell it.
to: A bank is considering a loan application from a manufacturer whose business plan reports capacity utilisation of 88%. Identify the questions the bank should ask about that figure before relying on it, and explain what each one would tell it.
why: Set out and say are not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Identify and Explain. Several questions are asked for, so no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: Namib Dairy Foods delivers to 140 shops from nine refrigerated vans of its own. Running the fleet costs N$918 000 a year in wages, fuel, licences and maintenance, all of which would end if the fleet were sold, and the vans would fetch about N$1 200 000. A national logistics firm offers to take the deliveries for N$6 300 a shop a year on a three-year contract. Two of the dairy's largest customers have said that same-day replacement of a damaged delivery is the reason they buy from it. Analyse the circumstances in which Namib Dairy Foods should outsource its distribution, and recommend what it should do.
to: Namib Dairy Foods delivers to 140 shops from nine refrigerated vans of its own. Running the fleet costs N$918 000 a year in wages, fuel, licences and maintenance, all of which would end if the fleet were sold, and the vans would fetch about N$1 200 000. A national logistics firm offers to take the deliveries for N$6 300 a shop a year on a three-year contract. Two of the dairy's largest customers have said that same-day replacement of a damaged delivery is the reason they buy from it. Analyse the circumstances in which Namib Dairy Foods should outsource its distribution, and evaluate what it should do.
why: Recommend is not used on the current AS papers; the judgement is now asked for with Evaluate. The card keeps its Analyse part, so it pairs the two parts of a Paper 1 Section B question (8 + 12) and no single paper tariff is claimed.
